'''Xizor's Palace''' was an enormous building on [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]] that belonged to [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]].

==History==
The [[Farfalla skyscraper]] was demolished for the construction.<ref name="CATCW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref>

Being Xizor's primary base of operations, he kept all his files on computers here.

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] [[Guri]] brought [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] to meet Xizor, asking for information about the assassination attempts against [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. Xizor was the one who wanted Luke dead, and although at first he welcomed the pair, Chewbacca uncovered his sinister role. He managed to escape (something that Xizor intended) while Leia remained prisoner in an opulent bedroom.

[[File:LandoNinja-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|left|180px|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] tosses the [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]] that will destroy the palace.]]
[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], [[Dash Rendar/Legends|Dash Rendar]], [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] [[Destruction of Xizor's Palace|infiltrated]] the palace through the [[sewers of Coruscant]] in an effort to rescue [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. They made it up into the castle, and defeated several guards before being confronted by Xizor and [[Guri]]. Calrissian and Skywalker forced the duo to back down with several [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]], threatening to set them off, destroying the palace.

Xizor retreated, but Calrissian dropped one of the explosives into a garbage chute that led down into the basement anyway. When it exploded, it destroyed the foundation of the building, sending it crumbling down to the surface. Xizor managed to escape in time, as did the heroes.

==Layout==
[[File:XizorPalaceGoSmash-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|right|180px|The ''Millennium Falcon'' escapes the exploding palace]]
The Palace was located in an area of the Imperial Center, making both the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]] and [[Darth Vader's Palace]] accessible through protected corridors.<ref name="secrets" /><ref name="sotes" /> It was an immense structure flanked by two exotic ornate towers.<ref name="sotes" /> According to [[Spero]], it was so majestic that it was comparable to the Emperor's and Vader's structures in the cityscape.<ref name="SEnovel">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref> 

It numbered around 120 levels, all traversed by [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolifts]] and access stairways, and mazes of corridors. 102 stories were above ground; the top floors were dedicated to Xizor's, and his guests's, residence, as well as audience chamber, meeting room, and communication and security center. These levels were protected by thick [[transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] ports that provided the Coruscanti cityscape to the residents and guests.<ref name="sotes" /> 

Xizor's chambers, office and audience hall had security monitoring equipment, as well as computers that accessed his massive information base (data about XTS and Black Sun, personal projects and blackmail files).<ref name="sotes" /> 

Xizor's personal spaces included exercise and combat training rooms, and a firing range. Other levels housed balroom chambers, gardens, receiving areas. False skylights gave light to internal courtyards. Some levels (such as level 50<ref name="SEnovel" />) had extended landing pads.<ref name="sotes" />

It had about 20 levels below ground. One of those housed a vault with the main [[Computer core/Legends|computer core]], which was connected to the terminals above with a main trunk line. The lowest level contained machinery for waste disposal and recycling.<ref name="sotes" /> As such, the lower levels connected to the [[Sewers of Coruscant|massive sewer system]] of the Imperial Center.<ref name="SEnovel" />

==Security==
The exterior and interior sections of the Palace were protected by vault-like [[blast door/Legends|blast doors]], locked with [[keypad]] [[code lock]]s, cardreader locks, and handprint scanners. A complex net-web connected [[comnet receiver]]s and [[Holocamera/Legends|holocams]] that surveyed every corner of the Palace. Additional monitoring units were in important rooms where Xizor frequented most, including the audience hall. Xizor maintained dedicated surveillance computers in his security center, and with his personal code, Xizor had full access to the net's records, but also was able to monitor security from any room.<ref name="sotes" />

[[Xizor's personal guards]] patrolled sections of the Palace. Their unofficial "[[captain/Legends|captain]]", who also oversaw their hiring and training, was [[Howzmin]], Xizor's chief of security and operations in the Palace. Howzmin's base was the Palace's surveillance information center, where he monitored various locations within, especially its network of repulsorlift tubeways connected to its entrances. He also coordinated Xizor's counter-[[spy/Legends|espionage]] [[agent/Legends|agents]] and was responsible for the blast door codes.<ref name="sotes" />

In his capacity as a gatekeeper, Howzmin expected Xizor's important guests outside the Palace, and sometimes personally he guided them (sometimes blindfolded) within.<ref name="sotes" />

Xizor's private quarters and office were not wired for surveillance and relied on guards' reports.<ref name="sotes" /> Furthermore communication failures happened frequently in some dead spots, because of pipes, conduits and thick heavy [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] beams, a problem the technicians could not resolve. However, drain sensors could report an invasion.

The computer core was sealed within a 7m-thick [[Duracrete/Legends|duracrete]] vault and beside the main trunk line, it was connected with emergency redundant access cables, some of them shielded against interferences. Xizor however opted not to maintain backup files of his database, to eliminate danger of its duplication.<ref name="sotes" />
==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I suppose the theme for Xizor's palace would be 'darkly majestic,' kind of evil and sinister but with a regal air about it. For the interior I concentrated on a lot of buttresses, arches, and some H.R. Gigeresque bioorganic stuff combined with Chinese inlaid engravings. With ancient Chinese architecture there are things like flowing lines with lighter contrasting to darker colors and interlocking lines. So I'd do a wall with that kind of inlaid Chinese border, and then below these flowing line patterns there'd be a steel archway with a bioorganic look.|[[Chris Hockabout]], texture artist for the [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' video game]]|<ref name="secrets" />}}
The 3d model of the Palace made for [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' video game]] incorporates various architectural styles such as a medieval fortress with gothic elements, and a "mystical, eastern look". Concept artist [[Paul Topolos]] was inspired by [[Ralph McQuarrie]]'s concept painting of the interior of the [[Imperial Palace]] during production of {{Film|6}}, which however was not filmed.<ref name="secrets">''[[The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]''</ref>
